newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N flat after five points drop, zloty up.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N flat after five points drop, zloty up.

text.p: Polish overnight rates stabilised at around 20 percent after a five point plunge from Wednesday's levels as banks refused to accept high rates on the first day of a new monthly average reserve period, dealers said.
They said players preferred to dig into their reserve accounts rather than seek cash on the market so there was no reason for rates to stay at Wednesday's highs.
"There is no reason for high overnight rates today - the first day of a new reserve period," said Marta Tabor from SA.
At 0845 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 19.8/20.2 percent against opening's 19.80/20.35 percent.

The zloty firmed slighlty against the basket of currencies after some dollar selling at 2.8120 zlotys, probably on the back of clients orders, stopped the early speculative downward pressure on the Polish unit, dealers said.
They said the zloty may continue firming especially if the dollar loses ground against the mark.

At 0940 GMT the zloty was traded at 1.87/1.81 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than 1.81/1.74 percent at opening. It was at 2.8110/25 per dollar, up from opening's 2.8126/35 and at 1.8590/00 to the mark, up from 1.8600/25.
